summary.title: At 31, I have just weeks to live. Here's what I want to pass on
summary.one_liner: A terminally ill 31-year-old shares five lessons he wants to leave behind: gratitude, living well, accepting vulnerability, helping others, and protecting the planet.
keywords: life is long enough if lived well
what matters at end of life
takeaways: Gratitude for family, friends and past experiences can help during the hardest moments of illness.
A life lived well can be full even if it is cut short; prioritise travel, movement and enjoyment.
Accepting vulnerability and help from others can strengthen relationships.
Growing older is a privilege, and doing something for others and for the planet matters.
Dying can be gentler than feared when medical care is supportive.
summary.summary: This is a personal essay published in The Guardian on the day its author, Elliot Dallen, died aged 31. It follows up his earlier piece about terminal cancer during lockdown, describing how his health declined, how a drug trial proved too harsh, and how his sister's return and his friends' support shaped his final months. The core of the piece is five things he wants others to take from his experience: gratitude, living a full life, accepting vulnerability, doing something for others, and protecting the planet. It ends with a note about a charity being set up in his memory.
